generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, a great deal of learning happens through doing: running a physiology test, analysing match footage, delivering a coaching session, working with a rehab client. The subjects differ in their evidence, lab data, training analysis, participation figures, clinical measures, but they share this. A cycle such as Experience, Reflect, Act gives it a shape, so a testing session that overran or a seminar that fell flat becomes something you deliberately learn from, rather than simply move past.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport and exercise science students write a short reflection after the same physiology practical, a VO2 max testing session that overran.

Tom writes that the session was stressful and the group ran out of time before everyone was tested, and resolves to be better organised next time. This touches an experience, but it does not work through it: there is no real reflection on why it overran, and the action, be better organised, is too vague to act on. Tom has stopped at the experience and jumped to a resolution.

Amara starts from the same experience, then reflects: the session overran because no one had set up the gas analyser before the first participant arrived, and the rush came from not having agreed who ran each station. From that, Amara settles on a concrete action, to calibrate and set up the equipment before the session and assign a station to each person. Experience, reflect, act: each stage done in turn.

Both wrote a reflection. Only Amara worked through the cycle, so only Amara came away with something usable.
generatedProse.summary: Structured reflection means working through an experience in set stages rather than at random, and a cycle such as Experience, Reflect, Act gives you those stages. You can now explain why a structure matters, recognise the stages at work in a sport example, and apply the cycle to one of your own experiences. The next lesson works on the stage that does the most work: reflecting, rather than only describing.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's reflection a worked-through cycle rather than a stalled one?

items.text: She reflected on why the testing session overran, then set a concrete action from it.
She wrote more about the session than Tom did.
She resolved to be better organised next time.
She found the session less stressful than Tom did.

feedback.correct: That's right. Reflecting on why it happened and then setting a concrete action is the cycle worked through.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara reflected on AND acted on, beyond the experience itself.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara worked through the cycle by reflecting on why it overran and setting a concrete action. Writing more, resolving vaguely or feeling calmer are not the same.
